newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ex-Argentine IBM chief turns himself in -- agency.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Argentine IBM chief turns himself in -- agency.

text.p: BUENOS AIRES, June 10 (Reuter ) - The former head of IBM Argentina, Ricardo Martorana, who faces bribery charges, turned himself in to the courts Tuesday, the state news agency Telam said.
Quoting court sources, the agency said Martorana was questioned by Judge Adolfo Bagnasco Tuesday night and was remanded in custody.

The judge, who is investigating the alleged corruption scandal involving the Argentine unit of International Business Machines Corp, two weeks ago asked Interpol to issue an arrest warrant for Martorana and three others indicted earlier this year in connection with the probe.
The judge suspects bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure International Business Machines Corp won a $250 million contract to install a computer system for the state bank Banco Nacion.
Martorana Tuesday denied being directly involved in the contract and apologized for having been a fugitive from justice, according to the sources quoted by Telam.

Martorana and former government and Banco Nacion officials have been charged with bribery. The former Banco Nacion president and deputy head, Aldo Dadone and Alfredo Aldaco, are also charged with embezzling public funds.
IBM has denied any wrongdoing, but admitted to errors "inconsistent with company policy." Other IBM contracts in Argentina have been the subject of separate bribery probes.
